contrarian_rules_for_day5.what_day1_actually_taught: The single Day-1 upset was a 2-0 with a 13-1 stomp on the opponent's own map pick - i.e. the market mispriced a single map, not a series collapse. Every other Day-1 series also ended 2-0, so 'fade the favorite' had no payoff on day one.
contrarian_rules_for_day5.what_day3_actually_taught: The same fixture reversed on four days' rest with the favorite picking the map it had just lost (Cache 13-11, then Inferno 13-4). Day-to-day team strength at this event was not unstable; the veto was.
usable_contrarian_conditions: Only fade a side when our OWN money-backed line disagrees with the crowd, never when Hotspawn '% picked' disagrees (Hotspawn popularity is excluded by rule 2 of the README and stays excluded).
The underdog must be >= 30% in our own no-vig probability AND the fixture must be worth 3+ Hotspawn points (tier b/c multipliers 1.5/1.0 x game multiplier 1.25 as published in the fixture API).
The crowd must NOT already be on the underdog: 10+ pickers on record with at least half on that side cannot move you past anyone.

At most 2 upset plays per UTC day, ranked by points x underdog probability x share-of-field passed, because Hotspawn scores correct picks only, so the expected cost of a contrarian play is points x (favorite - underdog probability).
contrarian_rules_for_day5.day5_specific: The TWC tournament pick'em Day-5 card is one Bo5. A Bo5 raises the favorite's series win rate for a given per-map edge, so a contrarian score-line (e.g. 3-1 BETBOOM) is a higher-variance, not a higher-edge, play. No probability, price or score-line is published here because no money-backed GF line was read in this session.
